Both these had good aggressive moves away from the DBD and RBR and provided good rejections on FTB, they were also both associated with significant Monthly SR levels. I thought I could use the level where supply overcame demand from the initial DBD/RBD to pinpoint where to enter as I had seen this working before, this seemed to work on the DBD but price did not reach this level on the RBD. Either way this was not accurate enough to place a pending order as the SL of the DBD would have been over 100 pips, even though the RR would have been good this is still too much. Hi Brox, don't worry, if you are new, just do one step at a time, in this case, focus on RBD and DBR first. We really don't trade those levels directly because this is what classic supply and demand traders do and as we know plain SD trading is just gambling with an (small) edge (IF). The purpose of this homework is to get a feel for basic market structure and to train your eye... And watch out for some tricks too (what happens on ignored levels on return and what happens on stacked levels). Price moves from supply to demand and vice versa. Once you study flag limits you will understand the relationship betweenthe RBD/DBR and FL concept

ps. to your question, it makes sense to mark all RBDs and DBRs strong or weak as long as the basic structure is present. BTW please check also the previous examples in this thread, could be helpful.
